I think a few more comments throughout the file could be useful.
This assumes /var/jenkins_home is present and writeable on the jenkins host node. Can we just use $HOME?
Fixed this and now all paths now derive from env.HOME resolved inside each node() block.

I'm curious about this, we've never needed this before, even when doing multiple bitbakes on a single build machine. Why is it needed now? I see a lot of complexity around this hash server and I'm not sure why we need it?

I figured we'd just start with the previous container (if available), build using the older containers sstate, and then run something like upstream-layers/openembedded-core/scripts/sstate-cache-management.py to clean out all the older sstates so we only have the most recent in the container.

Agreed and removed. Tested with just BB_SIGNATURE_HANDLER = "OEBasicHash" and hit 99% cache including nodejs/rust at the same commit. Hash server was unnecessary complexity and I used it initally due to extremely different commits upon pushing and pulling.
Why is a MIRROR needed?
MIRROR is only set for aarch64 nodes since they need ports.ubuntu.com (the ARM-specific Ubuntu mirror). x86 uses the default. Fixed to be conditional on arch.
This should be something like $nproc%4 (i.e. utilize 25% of systems processors).
I set BB_NUMBER_THREADS and PARALLEL_MAKE both set to nproc/4.
Why something special for nodejs?
Leftover from testing when the build was crashing.
Can we make a new Jenkins job for this?  I don't see the point in a adding a new trigger and then cutting out part of it for the trigger.
Done, made a new job for this.

Hmm, so this is going to use the local filesystem of our build nodes to remember when the last run occurred. I think we have an issue here in that any of our 8 nodes could get used. How do we ensure we have one node in charge of keeping track of time? There's no other way to do this without writing a persistent file? If not we probably need to use the https://jenkins.openbmc.org/label/built-in/ node for this time tracking.
Done, I just used built-in for time tracking.
Please move a bunch of this stuff to shell or python scripts.  There is way too much shell-like content in here to review adequately.
Done, Made 4 .sh files for better readability.
Jenkins provides a distinct "WORKSPACE" variable for each job, ensuring we don't run into conflicts. Any reason we're not using that as a part of our base?
Done, I was using the previous iteration because Yocto does not like the @ symbol but you informed me that you dealt with this before and changed that to an a.
Please provide comment on why this is needed. What if multiple containers are being built on the same system, any conflict issues with changing this global dir?
Done, I was concerned about compute/space but I should not worry about it until it becomes an issue.
More comments needed on what's going on here. The chown stuff seems a bit hacky.
Done, part of the shared dir and that was removed entirely.
nit: It's just Bitbake
Done
We don't have this in our main build CI. Certain issues in this path requiring retries?
Done, they were in place because the builds would fail due to out of memory issues but this would not happen outside of the local environment.
Could you add a high level comment on what this entrypoint.sh is for?
Done, added a comment to explain that it is there such that a UID is not baked in to the container.
Shell in shell in Jenkinsfile and Docker in shell in Jenkinsfile is ... a bit much.
Yeah, apologies made everything more readable.
Should this be unset? Don't want to echo the GHCR_TOKEN to the console.
Done, it was unset.
